expectations.text: A canonical model file exists separate from the generated JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: without_skill/outputs/model/airquality.model.yaml is the canonical model; the JSON Schema is generated separately to generated/airquality.schema.json by tools/generate.py.

expectations.text: Position is modelled as a value type without its own identity (a datatype, or explicitly marked as an embedded value without a key)
expectations.evidence: airquality.model.yaml defines Position under `classes:` ('Position: xml: {typeName: PositionType}') alongside Station etc., with no marker that it is a value type or embedded without identity. No text in the model, response.md or xsd-review.md calls it a value type or datatype; it is embedded only because the XSD nests it.

expectations.text: Pollutant is modelled as an extensible or externally governed code list, not a closed enum or an undocumented plain string
expectations.evidence: airquality.model.yaml SamplingPoint.pollutant is `type: string` with `json: {minLength: 1, examples: [NO2, PM10, ...]}` and the description copied from the XSD. It is not modelled as a code list (no enum or vocabulary entry). response.md: 'Tell me which six pollutants you receive and I'll add them as a code list ... did not enforce that.'

expectations.text: The station kind is modelled as a closed enumeration with traffic, industrial and background
expectations.evidence: airquality.model.yaml `enums: StationKind: values: traffic, industrial, background` (closed; emitted as xs:enumeration in the generated XSD and a JSON enum).

expectations.text: The meaning of the integer validity and verification codes is flagged as ambiguous
expectations.evidence: response.md Q6: 'What do `validity` and `verification` mean? They are bare integers with no code list.' xsd-review.md Q6 (High).

expectations.text: The missing coordinate reference system for lat/lon is flagged
expectations.evidence: response.md Q3: 'Which coordinate system? None is stated, and there are no range limits. I assumed WGS 84'; xsd-review.md Q3 'Coordinates without CRS (High)'.

expectations.text: Identifier issues are flagged (xs:ID values only unique within one document, and/or overlap of id and stationCode)
expectations.evidence: xsd-review.md Q1 '@id vs stationCode' and Q2: 'Uniqueness covers only one document. It says nothing about identity across files.' It also notes the ID space shared between stations and sampling points.

expectations.text: The observation volume (roughly 21 million per year: 400 x 6 x 24 x 365) is recorded in the canonical model, not only in prose
expectations.evidence: No volume figures in model/airquality.model.yaml (a grep for volume/million/57,600 finds nothing). Volume appears only in prose: response.md 'API shape (D1)' and xsd-review.md Q12 ('about 21 million/year').

expectations.text: The high observation volume leads to an API design note (e.g. observations as a separate, paginated resource rather than nested in station documents)
expectations.evidence: response.md D1: 'Use the nested ObservationCollection only for bulk ingest. For reads, serve /stations, /stations/{code}/sampling-points, a flat, paginated /observations?station=&pollutant=&from=&to=', motivated by about 21 million a year.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
expectations.evidence: Ran jsonschema Draft202012Validator.check_schema on generated/airquality.schema.json: OK. Instance with value null: 0 errors (value type [number, null]).

expectations.text: The JSON Schema keeps the observation value required but nullable, matching the XSD where the element is mandatory but nillable
expectations.evidence: Observation required includes 'value'; value type [number, null]. Tested: null is valid; key removed gives "'value' is a required property".

expectations.text: An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)
expectations.evidence: lxml (python -I): examples/sample.xml validates against the original (True) and generated/observations.xsd (True); a self-written minimal doc with nil value, validity 0, verification 7, no offset and an odd pollutant is also valid in both. A lat=95 doc is accepted by both (no tightening).

expectations.text: The pollutant code list is linked to a named standard vocabulary (e.g. the EEA/Eionet air quality pollutant vocabulary) with its register URI and a snapshot date or version, or reusing such a vocabulary is recommended to the user with the reason
expectations.evidence: The model has no vocabulary link for pollutant (only the description copied from the XSD). xsd-review.md Q5 cites http://dd.eionet.europa.eu/vocabulary/aq/pollutant/ only to note its numeric identifiers; the recommendation is to 'map them to a controlled list' and 'add them as an enum in the model', not to reuse or link the EEA vocabulary. No snapshot date or version. D3 lists 'code-list URIs for pollutant' only as a future partner-schema proposal, with no reason given.

claims.claim: The generated XSD is exactly as permissive as 2.1
claims.evidence: The sample, a minimal edge-case doc and a lat=95 doc all get identical verdicts.

claims.claim: The JSON Schema enforces the validity/verification code lists

suggestions.assertion: An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)
suggestions.reason: A single valid sample cannot detect tightenings. with_skill's generated XSD adds lat/lon range facets and rejects a lat=95 document the original accepts, yet still passes. Add edge-case documents (out-of-range lat, missing offset, unknown codes, nil altitude) or require that any tightening be explicitly disclosed.

suggestions.assertion: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
suggestions.reason: Both runs pass trivially, since a nullable value is the obvious mapping of nillable. Together with the 'required but nullable' assertion this is largely redundant.

No assertion checks whether the JSON Schema enforces assumed, unconfirmed code lists. without_skill enforces validity/verification enums in JSON (rejecting 2.1-valid data), while with_skill keeps them open. This meaningful design difference is not graded.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 4-7, 10 and 11 do not discriminate (both runs pass). The discriminating ones are Position as value type, pollutant code list, volume in the model, and vocabulary link.
